'''John Williamson''' (23 May 1901 – 1949) was a Scottish [[mathematician]] who worked in the fields of [[abstract algebra|algebra]], [[invariant theory]], and [[linear algebra]].  Among other contributions, he is known for the Williamson construction of [[Hadamard matrices]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Williamson, J.|title=Note on Hadamard's determinant theorem|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1947|volume=53|issue=6|pages=608–613|mr=0020538|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1947-08853-4|doi-access=free}}</ref>  Williamson graduated from the [[University of Edinburgh]] with [[first-class honours]] in 1922.  Awarded a newly established [[Commonwealth Fund Fellowship]] in 1925, he studied at the [[University of Chicago]] under the direction of [[Leonard Eugene Dickson|L. E. Dickson]] and [[E. H. Moore]], receiving the Ph.D. in 1927.  He held a Lectureship in Mathematics at the [[University of St Andrews]] and an Associate Professorship in Mathematics at [[Johns Hopkins University]].
